Voynich MS - Quire 20  

General

For an explanation of the material found on this page, see here.

Description

Quire 20 probably contained 7 normal-sized bifolia, of which the central bifolio is now missing. The remaining folios are numbered 103 through 108 and 111 through 116. The gathering mark is (unusually) on f103r.

This gathering contains the complete 'recipes' section. The section owes its name to the fact that it has short paragraphs preceded by a star each, and appear similar to recipes in medical MSs. The number of marginal stars is 324, but because (at least) one bifolio is missing, we don't know what would have been the total number.

Tiltman analysed the text of this section very intensively, and his conclusions have been summarised in the analysis section.

Theodore Petersen, in his hand transliteration, transcribed each paragraph on a single line (spanning several pages in width), hoping to find some indication of a similar structure in each paragraph.

  f116v  

>>Link to 2014 scan (Beinecke digital library)

>>Link to 2004 scan (Jason Davies Voyager)

General description

This is the last page of the MS, which follows none of the standard patterns, but has a few lines of text in a mixture of (apparent) Latin, German and writing in the Voynichese script, and some small marginal drawings. These have inspired many researchers, and led to long and so far inconclusive discussions.
There are a large hole and a tear in the upper left corner. The latter was stitched in the past.
There are numerous insect holes, also larger ones.

There are stains on this page which are from a previous tanned leather cover.

Illustration(s)

Three small drawings in the left margin, of (top down:) an indeterminate object, an animal and a possibly sitting nude woman.

Text

This page has 1 text item (locus) in the Voynich script, as follows:
1 pair of words, counted as a label of external writing.

These two words appear at the start of the last of four lines of writing near the top of the page. The first line is in the top margin, and the other three are in the normal text frame of the rest of the MS. The Voynich handwriting appears identical in all respects to that in the remainder of the MS.

Some people argue that in the left margin is another three-letter word in the latin (i.e. non-Voynich) alphabet.

Currier language: -
RZ language: - (page) / Bb (folio) / B+ (bifolio)
LFD hand: 3 (?)

Browse interlinear transliteration of f116v

Tentative identifications

The top marginal drawing has been considered to be some internal organ, perhaps a liver, but this is highly speculative. The second drawing is clearly an animal, not dissimilar in style to the Aries emblems in the zodiac. The first word on this page is widely considered to say "poxleber", a historical German word meaning 'goat liver', which is probably the main reason why the first item is considered by some to represent a liver.

The female figure either wears a cap or has some elaborate hairdo, and appears very similar in size and style to the figures (so-called 'nymphs') in the zodiac and biological sections.

The cleartext writing is very difficult to read, and many different interpretations have been offered. It appears to be a mixture of German and (pseudo-) Latin. The second and third lines have crosses in the shape of a 'plus' between the words, in a way similar to short prayers or incatations found in some manuscripts.

The last line appears to end with: "so nim geis mi(l)ch" (German for: "therefore take goat milk"). This reading was proposed already in the 1930's by Richard Salomon, and supported by Erwin Panofsky.

The handwriting of this extraneaous text is Gothic, and appears to be from the first half of the 15th century, as determined by Marco Ponzi and Koen Gheuens. In my personal view, the closest parallel is found in a 15th century manuscript in the Heidelberg library: Pal.Germ.647, which dates from 1445-1460.

Another (older) parallel is this IMAGE: 15th Century German alphabet table.

Other information

Goat liver can be found in classical recipes against night blindness.

People have considered that these few lines could just be pen trials.
